editorial.headline: IPTV Is a Telecom Service, Not Just a Screen
editorial.standfirst: For operators delivering interactive, quality-assured content convergence over IP, this activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity is for the operation of an Internet Protocol Television service: a telecommunications service that brings radio, television, video, audio, text, graphics and data together over an IP-based network. Its defining feature is not simply that content appears on a screen. The service is delivered as a converged offering, with stated assurance of service quality, security and reliability, and with two-way interactivity between provider and customer.

That makes the activity relevant to the operator running the telecommunications service itself. The scope describes a provider responsible for delivering the IP-based service and its interactive relationship with subscribers. Registration is open across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The scale range matters because the activity is framed as an operational telecommunications service, capable of being registered from the smallest listed category through to large enterprise.

Nationally, the foreign-ownership position is clear. The activity is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. In practical terms, foreign ownership may reach the full national ceiling recorded for this activity. That position is sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021; it is the national position, rather than a conclusion drawn from the Bali treatment.

Bali does not block PMA registration for this activity under its island-wide, permanent moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The record explains why: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the activity is not caught by that moratorium. For a foreign investor considering an IPTV operation in Bali, the honest reading is therefore not a blanket prohibition. Nationally the activity is open to 100% foreign ownership, and in Bali it is not blocked by the stated PMA moratorium because the recorded large-scale risk treatment sits above the categories the moratorium excludes.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally the activity is open to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali does not block it under the stated PMA moratorium.
